candidates.source_quality_note: Official USTR press release (archived, still resolves) is the best public market-learning source. Federal Register Proclamation 9694 (published 2018-01-25) is the legal action record.
candidates.anchor_convention_note: Anchor is 2018-01-22 close, the last close before the first positive market reaction. WHR showed no positive intraday reaction on 2018-01-22 (WHR -0.53% while XLY +1.10%). The v2.0 market-model h=1 of +3.64% was computed under OLS intercept+slope adjustment from the same anchor; the v2.1 production BHAR h=1 of +2.36% is the canonical claim. Both are significant; the difference is methodological.
candidates.restricted_because: Q4 2017 earnings released 2018-01-24 at 16:30 ET, after the 16:00 ET market close. First post-earnings session is 2018-01-25. h>=3 includes this session.
candidates.h2_diagnostic_note: h=2 (2018-01-22 close to 2018-01-24 close) is the maximum clean reaction window before earnings contamination. Reported as diagnostic only, not a claimed horizon.
candidates.peer_check_summary: No peer check required for WHR. WHR is the original Section 201 petitioner and the most directly exposed domestic washer producer. Unlike supply-shock candidates (where peer corroboration tests mechanism generality), the tariff-protection mechanism is specific to the petitioner.
candidates.caveat: h=1 and h=2 are clean. h>=3 is earnings-contaminated: Whirlpool Q4 2017 earnings were released 2018-01-24 at 16:30 ET (after the 16:00 ET market close); the first post-earnings session is 2018-01-25. h=5 (AR +7.70%, p=0.0003) and h=20 (AR +3.26%, p=0.44) include this contamination and must not be presented as tariff evidence. h=20 faded, which argues against any long-horizon momentum claim.
candidates.falsifier: WHR does not outperform XLY on 2018-01-23.

candidates.source_quality_note: Official US Army press release dated 2022-12-05. The Army page does not expose an exact publication timestamp in the audited source. A contemporaneous Breaking Defense article was published at 17:29 ET on Dec 5, supporting an after-close announcement convention. TXT showed no positive Dec 5 reaction and first priced the award on Dec 6.
candidates.anchor_convention_note: Anchor is 2022-12-05 close, the last close before the market could react. The Army FLRAA award page is dated Dec 5 but does not expose an exact publication timestamp in the audited source; a contemporaneous Breaking Defense article was published at 17:29 ET, supporting the after-close convention. First tradable reaction date is Dec 6.
candidates.restricted_because: No horizon-specific contamination identified. TXT Q4 2022 earnings were released 2023-01-25, outside the h=20 window. h=5 and h=20 are not statistically significant but are not restricted by a known confound.
candidates.peer_check_summary: TXT-vs-ITA sibling event study softens the paired-loser concern: TXT/ITA h=1 AR +7.09%, SAR +6.65, p < 0.001, larger than TXT/LMT +6.61%. The TXT/LMT result does not appear upward-biased relative to the TXT/ITA cross-check on h=1.
candidates.caveat: LMT is the PAIRED LOSER of the same news (Sikorsky/LMT lost FLRAA to Bell/TXT), not a neutral sector benchmark. Under production BHAR, AR_h1 = TXT_h1_return - LMT_h1_return = +5.25% - (-1.36%) = +6.61%; roughly +1.36% of that comes from LMT itself reacting in the opposite direction on the same news. A sector-ETF benchmark (e.g., ITA) would yield a smaller magnitude; conservative sector-equivalent AR point estimate is approximately TXT's own raw return of +5.25%. The h=5/h=20 flat reads (CAR ~+4%, both insignificant) are consistent with a contained one-time award option-value crystallization, not a weakness.
candidates.falsifier: TXT does not outperform LMT on 2022-12-06.

candidates.source_quality_note: Official Senate Democratic Leadership joint Schumer-Manchin statement dated 2022-07-27. The page identifies the IRA agreement and describes domestic energy/manufacturing and climate investment provisions. The source page does not expose an exact publication timestamp in the audited source; contemporaneous reporting supports an after-close/evening announcement convention.
candidates.anchor_convention_note: Anchor is 2022-07-27 close. The IRA agreement was announced after the July 27 regular-session close; the first regular-session tradable reaction date is July 28. The July 27 FOMC +75bp statement was released at 14:00 ET and is treated as an adjacent macro backdrop absorbed into the July 27 close, not as the event anchor.
candidates.restricted_because: FSLR Q2 2022 earnings were released after the 2022-07-28 regular-session close. h=1 ends at the July 28 close and is clean; h>=2 includes post-earnings trading and must not be presented as clean IRA evidence.
candidates.peer_check_summary: Clean-sector residual checks against XLU, XLI, and XLB, none containing FSLR, remain strongly positive on h=1: AR +11.71% to +13.53%, SAR +3.50 to +4.47. These checks support the h=1 policy-beneficiary reading while still requiring disclosure that the reaction was solar-sector-wide, not purely idiosyncratic.
candidates.caveat: h=1 only. h>=2 is earnings-contaminated (FSLR Q2 2022 released after the 2022-07-28 regular-session close). The July 27 FOMC +75bp decision is an adjacent macro backdrop absorbed into the July 27 anchor close, not a fatal confound; SPY +1.25% on July 28 captures continued FOMC interpretation, and the FSLR-specific component (AR +14.04% vs SPY) is an order of magnitude larger. Sector co-movement (TAN ~+5% same day) confirms the reaction is solar-sector-wide with FSLR as its strongest expression; not a unique idiosyncratic move.
candidates.falsifier: FSLR does not outperform SPY on 2022-07-28.

candidates.source_quality_note: Official Vale CEO press release on the Brumadinho dam breach, issued 2019-01-25. The press release confirms the dam breach but does not provide exact clock time. Independent technical reporting places the collapse at approximately 12:28 BRT / 10:28 ET, during US trading hours with roughly 5.5 hours remaining.
candidates.anchor_convention_note: Anchor is 2019-01-24 close, the last close before the Brumadinho dam collapse. The collapse occurred during US trading hours on 2019-01-25, so the first tradable reaction date is 2019-01-25.
candidates.restricted_because: No horizon-specific issuer earnings contamination identified. Rio Tinto 2018 full-year results were released 2019-02-27, outside the h=20 window. h=5 and h=20 are diagnostic only, not claimed.
candidates.peer_check_summary: BHP peer check is cache-backed after BHP backfill. BHP/SPY is directionally consistent with the iron-ore supply-shock mechanism: h=1 AR +2.56%, SAR +1.54, p=0.123; h=5 AR +7.38%, SAR +1.98, p=0.047; h=20 AR +10.56%, SAR +1.42, p=0.156. BHP corroborates direction but is weaker than RIO, consistent with greater diversification.
candidates.caveat: h=1 is the claimed horizon. RIO is a globally diversified miner (iron-ore ~70% of group EBITDA, plus aluminum, copper, diamonds, minerals); AR vs SPY captures the broad-market-adjusted move, not pure iron-ore exposure. RIO's h=1 SAR is the smallest in the cohort, consistent with this dilution. h=5 and h=20 are diagnostic: h=5 strengthened to +10.41% (p=0.002), h=20 plateaued at +12.05% (p=0.076), consistent with iron-ore price discovery over the first week then holding. BHP peer check is directionally corroborative (BHP h=1 AR +2.56%, same direction) but BHP h=1 is not individually significant (p=0.123), as expected from BHP's greater diversification.
candidates.falsifier: RIO does not outperform SPY on 2019-01-25.

candidates.source_quality_note: Official Commerce Department press release dated 2019-05-15 announcing addition of Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd. and affiliates to the Entity List. Federal Register 84 FR 22961 is the legal backup source. The Commerce source does not expose an exact publication timestamp in the audited source; local candidate history records an evening May 15 announcement, and the first full market reaction occurred May 16.
candidates.anchor_convention_note: Anchor is 2019-05-15 close. Commerce announced the Huawei Entity List action on May 15; local candidate history records the announcement as evening/after-close. Federal Register/BIS legal-publication timing falls later, but the market reaction tested here is to the May 15 Commerce announcement/news availability. First full equity session reflecting the news is May 16.
candidates.restricted_because: Lumentum issued a May 20, 2019 shipment/guidance update after the Huawei Entity List action. h=1 and h=2 are before that company-specific follow-up; h>=3, including h=5 and h=20, includes the May 20 update and must not be presented as clean Entity List announcement evidence.
candidates.h2_diagnostic_note: h=2 (2019-05-15 close to 2019-05-17 close) is the maximum clean reaction window before the May 20 Lumentum guidance/shipment update. Reported as diagnostic only, not a claimed horizon.
candidates.peer_check_summary: No peer check required for initial closeout. LITE has direct documented Huawei customer exposure; SMH sector benchmark absorbs broad semiconductor/Huawei supplier shock and likely makes the LITE-specific AR conservative. Optional future robustness could compare other Huawei-exposed suppliers, but not required for h=1 candidacy.
candidates.caveat: h=1 only. LITE had documented Huawei customer exposure of approximately 11% of revenue at the time of designation. h=2 is diagnostic (AR -15.07%, p < 1e-08) and clean. h>=3 is restricted by Lumentum's May 20, 2019 shipment/guidance update, which is a company-specific follow-up to the Entity List action. SMH is not a pure neutral benchmark because it also contains Huawei-exposed suppliers; this likely makes the LITE-specific residual conservative. The Huawei Entity List action was part of broader U.S.-China trade tensions; SMH absorbs the sector-wide component. The Oclaro acquisition closed December 2018; the estimation window sits entirely within the post-acquisition corporate form.
candidates.falsifier: LITE does not underperform SMH on 2019-05-16.

methodology_notes.event_study_form: Production BHAR via stats.event_study.compute_event_study. AR_h = (P_asset[t+h]/P_asset[t] - 1) - (P_bench[t+h]/P_bench[t] - 1) where t = event_index = the trading day BEFORE first_tradable_reaction_date. sigma_ar_daily = sample stddev (ddof=1) over the 60-bar pre-event estimation window. SAR_h = AR_h / (sigma_ar_daily * sqrt(h)). Daily simple close-to-close returns; auto_adjust=False.
methodology_notes.no_alpha_or_causality_claim: Nothing in this artifact constitutes a claim of causal mechanism, persistent edge, or replicable trading strategy. Each row reports a pre-registered direction, a measured abnormal return on a single named event, and a falsifier.
